qc.label_under_test: The noun stem 'nerve(s)' in any language (nerve, Nerven, nerveux/nerveuse, Korean 신경, Arabic عصبية), strongest in emotional idioms (nerve-racking, on my nerves) and weaker in the anatomical sense; not English 'nervous', not stress synonyms without the stem; minor side branch on ' strong' + noun. No hit/hurt branch.

neighbours.label: The stem 'nerve(s)' in its courage / stress / irritation sense, in any language (nerve-racking, the nerve to, nerves of steel, on my nerves, Nerven, nerveux/nerveuse); anatomical 'nerve' is near-silent, especially after an anatomical modifier (optic, sciatic, spinal, ulnar); not English 'nervous', not stress synonyms without the stem
fire: Giving my first speech in front of the board was truly nerve-racking.
You've got some nerve, talking to me like that after what you did.
The firefighter kept her nerve as the roof began to collapse.
His constant humming really gets on my nerves.
The goalkeeper has nerves of steel in penalty shootouts.
Das ständige Bellen geht mir wirklich auf die Nerven.
Elle était très nerveuse avant son premier concert.
It takes real nerve to quit a stable job and start a company.
quiet: The surgeon carefully repaired the damaged facial nerve after the accident.
Pressure on the ulnar nerve makes your fingers tingle.
The optic nerve connects the retina to the brain.
Der Ischiasnerv verläuft an der Rückseite des Beins.
Le nerf sciatique descend le long de la jambe.
Giving my first speech in front of the board was truly stressful.
She was very nervous before her first concert.
The spinal nerve roots were compressed by a herniated disc.
